answers.core: The various variant types are even more low-level than what GDExtensions could possibly access. Therefore, this must be a core proposal and not an asset library proposal.
answers.workaround:
[TL;DR: no]

* One could cache the extension language counterparts to partially mitigate the redundancy issue, but that explicitly deals with one of the `10` hard things in Computer Science.
* Extension classes can define an internal property that stashes the extension counterpart’s `userdata` such as an ID.
  Howëver, this customization is not available to builtin classes and other extensions’ classes, let alone non-`Object` variants. (Unless you tell me that I can open them up willy-nilly this whole time.)
  * The same strategy applies to `ScriptExtension`s as well and they can even enhance arbitrary `Object`s.
    But what if said objects already has scripts? Multi-script `Object`s aren’t a thing for the forseeable future, and so aren’t non-`Object` variants with scripts.

An API universal to all variants also benefits extension classes and `ScriptExtension`s by ~~*extension*~~ inheritance.

title: GDExtension Custom Bindings (i.e., `userdata`) for Other Variant Types (in addition to `Object`)
